svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: iOS · Interval grading viewer · Text tab · Add Crafted Text · portrait
svg.desc:
Mirrors App/Overlay/CraftedTextSheet.swift as raised on iPhone from App/Overlay/OverlayEditingPanel.swift's craftButton — NEW 2026-09-04 from the Claude Design handoff "Photo viewer text transitions" TURN 3. The handoff's iPhone file was NOT re-exported for turns 3 and 4 (it is byte-identical to the version already shipped), so this treatment is DERIVED, not drawn: the sheet is the Mac card's content at touch sizes in the dark editor idiom, agreed with Steven on 2026-09-04 before the build.
PRESENTATION: a sheet with [.medium, .large] detents and a visible drag indicator, forced to .preferredColorScheme(.dark) over LL.ink — the Text tab is the dark full-screen cover, and a sheet raised from it that came up white would look like a different app (it did, on the first simulator run). Content is top-aligned with a trailing Spacer so the brief field cannot stretch to fill the screen; the field is a FIXED height (88 in the prompt state, 96 here) for the same reason.
DRAWN HERE: the SIMPLE state, which is what an iPhone with no LANGUAGE model installed opens — the state the 16 Pro simulator showed on 2026-09-04, where the active catalogue entry was the built-in Vision tagger. Only an MLX entry counts as available (Vision tags scenes and the Core ML entry segments them; neither can write a word), so this state is not an error, it is the honest offer: one line per layer, in the user's own words, laid out and linked exactly as the model's answer would be. Header ✦ CRAFTED TEXT (11/700 +0.5, white 55%) and a 22pt ✕ disc on #2C2C2E; title "Add text" 19/700; the helper line 12pt white 55%; the field (96 tall, radius 8, 1px white-22% border, 14pt, the two-line placeholder); the notice row (amber 8%, radius 10: ✦ "Enable AI to enhance this experience" and "Settings › AI Models ›" 11.5/600 amber); and the Add pill (32pt, amber, #1C1C1E label, 40% while the field is empty) reading "Add line" or "Add N lines".
THE OTHER THREE STATES are the Mac's, at these sizes — see macOS/photo-viewer.text.crafted.svg for the prompt, thinking and candidates states and for what is done with the parts that come back. WHAT LANDS: LL_TEXT=crafted stages the result on this simulator — the brief "A little sand between your toes helps wash away the woes" through the splitter, the layout and the insert — and it lands as two layers, "Crafted · line 1" (white, the longest word lemon) and "Crafted · line 2" (the payoff: amber, larger, Element · Pop), the second following the first, both fitted to 84% of the frame and stacked on 0.56 of its height. The badge on the picture then reads "Crafted · line 1 · +1 follows".

g.text: One line per layer. Lines stack top to bottom and follow
A little sand between your toes
With a language model installed this opens on the PROMPT state instead:
"What would you like to communicate?", Final copy · Needs work, Send.
